items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: I have one record home now I made with Jelly Roll... during the time we were playing at the Rose Danceland... we went down in Pennsylvania to the coal regions... we played

ctx.x: They weren't really that old then.

Well, they were older than I was, you know. I don't know how old -- I was about 17, 18, 19. They were probably 25. I called them old, you know. Yeah. So anyway, when I discovered Jelly Roll, you know, he -- I realized that he really had something, you know, his style and his music and his -- and I have one record home now I made with Jelly Roll. I was just playing it last week. I made it in must have been '28, '28 when I --

items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: I have it that you were with Charlie Skeets in '27 and that you worked with Jelly Roll Morton in the summer of '28. So would that be part of '27 and into '28? ... Yeah, I guess so, yeah.

ctx.x: And it was called Jelly Roll Morton's orchestra?
Jelly Roll Morton and his Red Hot Peppers.
Oh, it was the Red Hot Peppers.

items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: I don't know just how many. Maybe 15 Jellyroll Morton tunes, you know.

ctx.x: But did the band play hits of the

Oh, no, no, of course not, no. Like the band played about -- I don't know just how many. Maybe 15 Jellyroll Morton tunes, you know. But as I remember he had an audience even then because they'd come up and request things that they had heard on records by Jellyroll, you know. And he didn't have Simon then. Simon didn't go on the trip. I think he went back home to Chicago. And of course I didn't know all of them, you know, because Simon used to play them. I did the best I could with the clarinet work. So that came…
Then you went to another dance school.
